For $p=2$, the preceding strong well-posedness theorem gives the stronger

global strong solution supplied by

$p\ge2$ with $E|X_0|^p<\infty$, the unique solution satisfies
$$\sup_{0\le t\le T}E|X_t|^p\le 2^{p/2}(1+E|X_0|^p)e^{C_pT},\qquad C_p:=\sqrt2\,pK+p(p-1)K^2.$$
The supremum is over the individual-time moments; for $p>2$ this statement
does not assert an $E\sup_{t\le T}|X_t|^p$ bound. In particular, if $X_0$
has every finite moment of order $p\ge2$, then the solution has uniform
finite-horizon moments of every such order.

## Statement

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). In a proper Bayesian model, suppose both parameter and data spaces $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$ and $(\mathsf Y,\mathcal Y)$ are standard Borel ([[def-standard-borel-space]]). Let $J$ be the joint prior-predictive law and let $J_Y$ be its data marginal. There is a data-indexed posterior probability kernel $y\mapsto\Pi_y$ such that, for all $A\in\mathcal T$ and $B\in\mathcal Y$,
$$J(A\times B)=\int_B\Pi_y(A)\,J_Y(dy),\qquad J_Y(B)=\int_\Theta K(\theta,B)\,\Pi(d\theta).$$
The composition $\Pi_{Y(\omega)}$ is a posterior RCD. Any two data-indexed posterior kernels agree as probability measures outside one measurable $J_Y$-null set; their values at null data values are not pointwise determined.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A proper Bayesian model, its prior-predictive joint law $J$, the parameter and data coordinate maps $X,Y$, AC, and standard-Borel parameter and data spaces.

[A1] The Axiom of Choice (AC). [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The prior and parameter-measurable sampling kernel define the joint probability $J$ and its rectangle law. [[lem-prior-and-model-kernel-define-joint-law]]

[F2] Coordinate projections have measurable inverse images because they are measurable rectangles; a measurable map into a probability space is a random element. [[def-product-sigma-algebra-and-finite-product-sigma-algebras]], [[def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces]], [[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]

[F3] A posterior RCD exists when the parameter space is standard Borel, with no standard-Borel requirement on the data space. [[cor-posterior-r-c-d-exists-for-standard-borel-parameter]]

[F4] If both random-element targets are standard Borel and AC holds, an RCD of $X$ given $\sigma(Y)$ factors through $Y$ as a probability kernel on the data space. [[lem-regular-conditional-kernels-factor-through-a-standard-borel-conditioning-variable]]

[F5] A data-indexed probability kernel is a conditional law precisely when its composition with $Y$ satisfies the conditional event identities. [[def-conditional-law-given-a-random-element]]

[F6] A joint probability on a product of standard-Borel spaces admits a disintegration kernel, unique outside one null set of its second marginal. [[thm-disintegration-of-a-joint-law-on-standard-borel-spaces]]

## Proof

**Given:** The model and hypotheses in the statement.

1.1 By [F1], $J$ is a probability measure on $(\Theta\times\mathsf Y,\mathcal T\otimes\mathcal Y)$ and $J_Y(B)=J(\Theta\times B)=\int_\Theta K(\theta,B)\,\Pi(d\theta)$. Its coordinate maps $X$ and $Y$ are measurable by [F2]. [given, F1, F2, construct]

2.1 Since $\Theta$ is standard Borel and [A1] holds, [F3] supplies a posterior RCD $L$ of $X$ given $\sigma(Y)$ on the canonical space of step 1.1. [given, A1, F3, step 1.1, choose]

3.1 Both $\Theta$ and $\mathsf Y$ are standard Borel and [A1] holds, so [F4] factors $L$ through $Y$ as a probability kernel $\Pi_y$; hence its evaluations are $\mathcal Y$-measurable and every section is a probability. By [F5], the composition $\Pi_Y$ is a conditional law, with rectangle identity $J(A\times B)=\int_B\Pi_y(A)\,J_Y(dy)$. [given, A1, F4, F5, step 2.1]

4.1 Apply [F6] to the same joint probability $J$. It gives uniqueness of the disintegration kernel as a probability measure outside one $J_Y$-null set. Thus the posterior is specified up to that null set, not at each null data value. [A1, F6, step 1.1, step 3.1] ∎

row-vector process [[def-progressively-measurable-and-predictable-process]] with
$\mathbb E\int_0^T\|H_s\|_2^2ds<\infty$. For

## Statement

Assume AC and the finite-$L^2$ coefficient and initial-value hypotheses of
[[thm-euler-maruyama-strong-rate-for-square-integrable-initial-data]]. Fix an
integer refinement factor $M\ge2$ and a fine step $h$ with $0<h\le1/M$,
$T/h\in\mathbb N$, and $T/(Mh)\in\mathbb N$. Construct the fine and coarse
Euler paths with the same initial value and Brownian motion. The coarse
Brownian increment over each coarse interval is, by definition, the sum of
the $M$ fine Brownian increments in that interval. Let $X_T$ be the common
exact solution, and let $\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ be globally
Lipschitz with constant $L_\varphi$. Then constants independent of $h$ satisfy
$$ \mathbb E|Y_T^h-Y_T^{Mh}|^2\le C_M h, $$
$$ \operatorname{Var}\bigl(\varphi(Y_T^h)-\varphi(Y_T^{Mh})\bigr)\le C_ML_\varphi^2h, \qquad |\mathbb E\varphi(X_T)-\mathbb E\varphi(Y_T^h)|\le C L_\varphi h^{1/2}. $$
Thus the Lipschitz-payoff Euler level pair has correction variance exponent
$\beta=1$ and strong-error bias exponent $\alpha=1/2$. If, in addition,
$\varphi$ is bounded and its backward value function satisfies the hypotheses
of [[thm-euler-maruyama-weak-order-one-under-backward-regularity]], then the
bias bound improves to $|\mathbb E\varphi(X_T)-\mathbb E\varphi(Y_T^h)|\le Ch$,
so $\alpha=1$ while $\beta=1$ remains. With fixed dimension, fixed $M$, and
unit-cost coefficient and payoff evaluations, one coupled fine/coarse sample
has work $O(h^{-1})$.

**Given:** AC; the stated finite-$L^2$ SDE assumptions; the fixed refinement factor and nested grids; a common exact solution and Brownian path; and the Lipschitz payoff (plus, for the weak branch, the bounded-payoff backward contract).

[F1] Under the finite-$L^2$ coefficient, time-modulus, Brownian and initial-value hypotheses, the continuous Euler path satisfies $\mathbb E\sup_{t\le T}|X_t-Y_t^h|^2\le Ch$, uniformly in $0<h\le1$ with $T/h\in\mathbb N$. [[thm-euler-maruyama-strong-rate-for-square-integrable-initial-data]]

[F2] For the weak-bias branch, retain finite $d,m$, the Euclidean/Frobenius norm convention and $A:B=\operatorname{tr}(A^{\mathsf T}B)$, and the same finite-horizon, complete usual filtered Brownian and grid setup as in the Statement. Assume jointly Borel coefficients that are globally Lipschitz in state, have uniform linear growth, and satisfy the half-Hölder time modulus. Require an $\mathcal F_0$-measurable initial value independent of future Brownian increments with $\mathbb E|X_0|^p<\infty$ for finite real $q\ge0$ and finite $p\ge2q+8$ (using $|x|^0=1$), and uniform pointwise order-$p$ moments of the exact solution, Euler interpolation, and Euler step process on $[0,T]$. The payoff is bounded Borel, and its backward value function $u(t,x)=\mathbb E[\varphi(X_T^{t,x})]$, using the unique shifted strong solutions supplied by the global well-posedness theorem, satisfies $u(T,x)=\varphi(x)$, $(\partial_t+L_t)u=0$ for $L_tv=b(t,\cdot)\cdot\nabla v+\tfrac12(\sigma\sigma^{\mathsf T})(t,\cdot):D_x^2v$, and continuous mixed derivatives $\partial_t^jD_x^\alpha u$ for $0\le j\le2$, $|\alpha|\le4$, bounded by $C_u(1+|x|^q)$. Under this full contract of [[thm-euler-maruyama-weak-order-one-under-backward-regularity]], $|\mathbb E\varphi(X_T)-\mathbb E\varphi(Y_T^h)|\le Ch$.

[A1] The refinement factor $M$ is fixed as $h\to0$; both mesh sizes obey $0<h\le1$ and have $T/h$ and $T/(Mh)$ integral. The coarse path uses the sum of each corresponding block of $M$ fine Brownian increments, so both Euler paths use the same Brownian path and initial value.

[A2] $|\varphi(x)-\varphi(y)|\le L_\varphi|x-y|$ for all states. In the weak branch, the same $\varphi$ is bounded and satisfies the additional backward regularity contract [F2].

[A3] AC is included because [F1] carries that assumption from the Doob and Brownian Itô interfaces. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

## Statement

Assume AC and the finite-$L^2$ coefficient and initial-value hypotheses of
[[thm-euler-maruyama-strong-rate-for-square-integrable-initial-data]]. Fix an
integer refinement factor $M\ge2$ and a fine step $h$ with $0<h\le1/M$,
$T/h\in\mathbb N$, and $T/(Mh)\in\mathbb N$. Construct the fine and coarse
Euler paths with the same initial value and Brownian motion. The coarse
Brownian increment over each coarse interval is, by definition, the sum of
the $M$ fine Brownian increments in that interval. Let $X_T$ be the common
exact solution, and let $\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ be globally
Lipschitz with constant $L_\varphi$. Then constants independent of $h$ satisfy
$$ \mathbb E|Y_T^h-Y_T^{Mh}|^2\le C_M h, $$
$$ \operatorname{Var}\bigl(\varphi(Y_T^h)-\varphi(Y_T^{Mh})\bigr)\le C_ML_\varphi^2h, \qquad |\mathbb E\varphi(X_T)-\mathbb E\varphi(Y_T^h)|\le C L_\varphi h^{1/2}. $$
Thus the Lipschitz-payoff Euler level pair has correction variance exponent
$\beta=1$ and strong-error bias exponent $\alpha=1/2$. If, in addition,
$\varphi$ is bounded and its backward value function satisfies the hypotheses
of [[thm-euler-maruyama-weak-order-one-under-backward-regularity]], then the
bias bound improves to $|\mathbb E\varphi(X_T)-\mathbb E\varphi(Y_T^h)|\le Ch$,
so $\alpha=1$ while $\beta=1$ remains. With fixed dimension, fixed $M$, and
unit-cost coefficient and payoff evaluations, one coupled fine/coarse sample
has work $O(h^{-1})$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC; the stated finite-$L^2$ SDE assumptions; the fixed refinement factor and nested grids; a common exact solution and Brownian path; and the Lipschitz payoff (plus, for the weak branch, the bounded-payoff backward contract).

[F1] Under the finite-$L^2$ coefficient, time-modulus, Brownian and initial-value hypotheses, the continuous Euler path satisfies $\mathbb E\sup_{t\le T}|X_t-Y_t^h|^2\le Ch$, uniformly in $0<h\le1$ with $T/h\in\mathbb N$. [[thm-euler-maruyama-strong-rate-for-square-integrable-initial-data]]

[F2] For the weak-bias branch, retain finite $d,m$, the Euclidean/Frobenius norm convention and $A:B=\operatorname{tr}(A^{\mathsf T}B)$, and the same finite-horizon, complete usual filtered Brownian and grid setup as in the Statement. Assume jointly Borel coefficients that are globally Lipschitz in state, have uniform linear growth, and satisfy the half-Hölder time modulus. Require an $\mathcal F_0$-measurable initial value independent of future Brownian increments with $\mathbb E|X_0|^p<\infty$ for finite real $q\ge0$ and finite $p\ge2q+8$ (using $|x|^0=1$), and uniform pointwise order-$p$ moments of the exact solution, Euler interpolation, and Euler step process on $[0,T]$. The payoff is bounded Borel, and its backward value function $u(t,x)=\mathbb E[\varphi(X_T^{t,x})]$, using the unique shifted strong solutions supplied by the global well-posedness theorem, satisfies $u(T,x)=\varphi(x)$, $(\partial_t+L_t)u=0$ for $L_tv=b(t,\cdot)\cdot\nabla v+\tfrac12(\sigma\sigma^{\mathsf T})(t,\cdot):D_x^2v$, and continuous mixed derivatives $\partial_t^jD_x^\alpha u$ for $0\le j\le2$, $|\alpha|\le4$, bounded by $C_u(1+|x|^q)$. Under this full contract of [[thm-euler-maruyama-weak-order-one-under-backward-regularity]], $|\mathbb E\varphi(X_T)-\mathbb E\varphi(Y_T^h)|\le Ch$.

[A1] The refinement factor $M$ is fixed as $h\to0$; both mesh sizes obey $0<h\le1$ and have $T/h$ and $T/(Mh)$ integral. The coarse path uses the sum of each corresponding block of $M$ fine Brownian increments, so both Euler paths use the same Brownian path and initial value.

[A2] $|\varphi(x)-\varphi(y)|\le L_\varphi|x-y|$ for all states. In the weak branch, the same $\varphi$ is bounded and satisfies the additional backward regularity contract [F2].

[A3] AC is included because [F1] carries that assumption from the Doob and Brownian Itô interfaces. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]
